genre.puzzle.titre_seo: Free puzzle and logic games for kids to play online
genre.puzzle.description_seo: Brain teasers, pieces to put back in place and logic riddles to solve at your own pace: free games for kids on phone, tablet or PC, then offline.
genre.puzzle.intro: Here, you play with your head rather than with fast fingers. You put pieces back where they belong, slide blocks, connect shapes or find the only solution that works. Most of the time there's no rush: you can look, try, make mistakes and start again as many times as you like. With each riddle you solve, your reasoning gets stronger, and so does your patience; you also learn to picture things in space and to plan one move ahead. Some brain teasers can be solved from age 5 or 6, while others give players aged 9 and up a real challenge. A tip for when you're stuck: explain out loud what you've already tried. Saying it often shows you what's missing.

genre.memoire.titre_seo: Free memory games for kids: matching pairs and sequences
genre.memoire.description_seo: Find the matching pairs, remember sequences of colors and sounds: free memory games for kids on a computer, tablet or phone, then offline too.
genre.memoire.intro: Turn over two cards and remember what they were hiding, repeat a sequence of colors or sounds, spot the object that has moved: your memory is put to the test, round after round. At first there's only a little to remember, then the list grows bit by bit, until you really have to concentrate. This trains working memory, the kind you also use to keep an instruction or a lesson in your head. Simple picture pairs are within reach of 3- and 4-year-olds; older kids will be more interested in beating their record. Pass the screen around at each turn and the game quickly becomes a little challenge at home, and the grown-up doesn't always win.

genre.quiz.titre_seo: Free quizzes for kids: general knowledge trivia questions
genre.quiz.description_seo: Test your general knowledge one question at a time on a phone, tablet or computer: free trivia quizzes for kids that you can replay offline later.
genre.quiz.intro: A quiz is a question, several possible answers and a moment of suspense before you find out if you got it right. Questions can be about nature, countries, animals, sports, history or everyday life. Getting it wrong is no big deal: an answer you discover after a mistake often sticks better in your memory. You need to read carefully and think before you choose, and your curiosity grows with every round of questions. These games are mainly for independent readers, around 7 or 8; for younger kids, a grown-up can read the questions out loud and team up with the child. And when a question stumps you, why not look up the answer together in a book or a dictionary?

genre.mots.titre_seo: Free online word and letter games for kids: spelling fun
genre.mots.description_seo: Put the letters in order, guess the hidden word: free letter and vocabulary games on a phone, tablet or PC, which you can then play offline.
genre.mots.intro: With word and letter games, language becomes a playground. You put letters in the right order, guess a hidden word, complete a sentence or hunt for words in a grid. Without feeling like you're doing schoolwork, you learn to recognize letters, spell words better and build your vocabulary. Games where you catch or match letters support the first steps in reading, from age 4 or 5; longer grids and rarer words will appeal to readers aged 9 and up. An unfamiliar word you come across during a game can become the word of the day, which everyone at home tries to slip into a sentence before evening.

genre.calcul.titre_seo: Free online math games for kids: counting and times tables
genre.calcul.description_seo: Count, add up, practice your times tables: free math and number games for kids on a tablet, phone or PC, and playable offline after your first game.
genre.calcul.intro: In these games, numbers become things to pick up, coins to give as change, boxes to fill in or a race against the clock. Counting, adding up to reach the right total, comparing two numbers, solving a little problem: each right answer moves the game forward, and math becomes very concrete. Mental math, number sense and reasoning improve through repetition. Around 4 or 5, you start by counting and recognizing digits; times tables and bigger calculations usually come from age 7 or 8. A few short, regular sessions are better than one long session that wears you out, and a sum from the game is easy to redo with real objects, like pasta or buttons.

genre.reflexes.titre_seo: Free reflex games for kids: test your reaction speed
genre.reflexes.description_seo: Tap the target before it gets away, catch what falls, dodge: free reflex games for kids on a smartphone, tablet or PC, and offline afterwards.
genre.reflexes.intro: Everything happens in a split second. Tap a target before it disappears, react as soon as a color changes, catch what's falling, or on the contrary hold your finger back when you mustn't touch: these games put your reaction speed to the test. Rounds are often short, which makes you want to play again right away to grab a few more points, and the pace usually speeds up from level to level. What improves: speed, coordination between what your eyes see and what your finger does, and the ability to stay focused despite all the action. Since there's little to read, the simplest ones work for kids around 4 or 5. These games are intense: after a few rounds, a break to catch your breath does you good.

genre.arcade.titre_seo: Free arcade games for kids: quick to learn, ready to play
genre.arcade.description_seo: Rules you understand in seconds and the urge to play again: free arcade games for kids on a phone, tablet or PC, and offline afterwards too.
genre.arcade.intro: Arcade games keep the spirit of the game machines of the past, found in cafés and arcades: a rule you understand in a few seconds, a game that starts right away, and the urge to start again to get a little further. You catch, dodge, bounce or collect bonuses, often with a difficulty that rises gently. When the screen gets busy, skill and a cool head make the difference. Little text and simple controls by finger or keyboard: most of these games are easy to pick up around age 5, sometimes earlier. Their short format fits easily into a little break between two activities.

genre.plateforme.titre_seo: Free platform games for kids: run, jump and climb online
genre.plateforme.description_seo: Run, jump over the gaps and climb to the finish: platform games played by finger on phones and tablets or with the keyboard on PC, then offline.
genre.plateforme.intro: Your character runs, jumps and climbs through a world full of obstacles. The goal: reach the end of the level without falling into gaps or touching traps, collecting shiny things along the way. It's all about timing. Jump too early or too late, and you have to start over, a little smarter than the time before. Attempt after attempt, your moves become more precise, you learn to anticipate and you discover what it means to persevere. These games often appeal from age 6 or 7, when handling several controls at once comes easily. Missing a jump is part of the game: every fall teaches you where to put your feet next time.

genre.course.titre_seo: Free racing games for kids: beat the clock on every track
genre.course.description_seo: Take the bends at the right moment and speed toward the finish line: free racing games for kids on a phone, tablet or PC, even offline later.
genre.course.intro: First across the finish line or faster than the clock: that's the goal. Depending on the game, you drive a vehicle, make an animal gallop or run yourself, taking each bend carefully and avoiding whatever slows you down. You discover the track as you go, and each attempt helps you spot the best lines. Reflexes, anticipation and control of small movements, by finger or keyboard, get sharper lap after lap. Races where you only need to steer suit kids from 5 or 6; more technical courses are aimed more at ages 8 and up. A good driver knows the track by heart: running the same course again to shave off a few tenths of a second teaches you to improve step by step.

genre.sport.titre_seo: Free sports games for kids: matches and events to play
genre.sport.description_seo: Score a goal, jump at the right moment, beat your best time: free sports games for kids on a smartphone, tablet or PC, then offline as well.
genre.sport.intro: On the field, on the track, on the snow or on the mat, sports are played right on the screen here. You aim for the goal, jump at the right moment, string moves together or try to beat your best time, while following the rules of the sport. Accuracy, a sense of rhythm and a taste for challenge all come into play, and along the way you understand how a match or an event works. What counts is the action: you play the event itself, with its moves and its clock. From 5 or 6, you can already score your first points; technical events take more practice, just like in real life. A tip for every champion: nothing beats a real ball and some fresh air afterwards.

genre.tir.h1: Aiming games: target shooting and skill
genre.tir.titre_seo: Free target shooting and aiming games for kids to play
genre.tir.description_seo: Set the power and the angle, then aim for the bull's-eye: free, non-violent target games for kids on a phone, tablet or computer, then offline.
genre.tir.intro: Aiming well matters more than anything. You throw a ball, a dart or a bubble at a target, choose the power and the angle, then watch where your shot lands to correct the next one. No realistic violence: you aim at targets, balloons, bubbles or objects. These skill games build concentration and a feel for trajectories. Without knowing it, you even take your first steps in physics, watching a ball rise, slow down and fall back. They're played from about age 6; shots with bounces or wind take more thinking and appeal to older kids. The best practice? Calmly working out why a shot missed, rather than trying again at random.

genre.combat.titre_seo: Fighting games for kids: fun, free and friendly duels
genre.combat.description_seo: Dodge, block and pick the right moment: duels for kids with no realistic violence, free on a computer, tablet or phone, and offline later on.
genre.combat.intro: A duel where skill and cunning count more than strength: that's the idea. You dodge, block and wait for the right moment to act. The opponent is often a funny character or an imaginary creature, pushed back or sent out of play, with no realistic violence and no really scary scenes. Fighting can also take the form of a sport, like judo, with its throws, its bow and respect for your partner. You need reflexes, a sharp eye on your opponent and calm in tense moments. It's better to be 6 or 7 to enjoy them fully. Win, lose, bow and play again: these games are a great chance to talk about fair play and self-control.

genre.labyrinthe.titre_seo: Free maze games for kids: find your way to the exit
genre.labyrinthe.description_seo: Find the exit! Corridors, dead ends and crossroads in free maze games for kids on a phone, tablet or computer, then offline once you've opened them.
genre.labyrinthe.intro: Which way leads to the exit? That's the whole question. You guide a character or a marble through a tangle of corridors, avoiding dead ends, sometimes picking up objects or opening doors with the right key. As the levels go on, the paths usually get more complicated. Looking at the map before rushing in often saves time: that's the whole point of these games, which train your sense of direction, planning and patience. Small mazes are within reach of 4- and 5-year-olds; big winding mazes are more for explorers aged 8 and up. For the very young, tracing the path with a finger first, without playing, helps them think ahead.

genre.aventure.titre_seo: Free adventure and exploration games for kids online
genre.aventure.description_seo: Explore an island or a castle, find useful objects, solve riddles: free adventure games on a phone, tablet or computer, then playable offline.
genre.aventure.intro: What lies beyond the next passage? In an adventure game, curiosity keeps you moving. You explore an island, a forest, a castle or a faraway planet, meet characters, pick up objects and find out where each one becomes useful. Little by little, the clues connect and the story moves on. Logic, memory for places and reading are needed at every step. These games are mainly for kids who read on their own, around 6 or 7; younger ones enjoy discovering them with someone by their side. With two players, one at the controls and the other as the adviser, exploring becomes even livelier.

genre.observation.titre_seo: Free hidden object and observation games to play online
genre.observation.description_seo: Hidden objects, spot the difference, find the odd one out: observation games where every detail counts, on phone, tablet or PC, offline later.
genre.observation.intro: Open your eyes wide: everything is hidden in the details. You need to find objects tucked away in a picture, spot the differences between two almost identical drawings or track down the odd one out that doesn't belong. You look closely, then tap the exact spot. Visual attention and concentration get sharper, and you learn to examine a scene methodically, from left to right or corner by corner. Since there's almost nothing to read, simple pictures suit kids from 3 or 4; busy scenes will appeal to older ones. Naming each object you find, alone or with a grown-up, also builds the vocabulary of the youngest players.

genre.strategie.titre_seo: Free strategy games for kids who love to think ahead
genre.strategie.description_seo: Anticipate your opponent's moves and choose the right plan: free strategy games for kids on a phone, tablet or PC, and playable offline afterwards.
genre.strategie.intro: Luck counts for little: here, everything depends on the decisions you make. You place your pieces, choose which way to go, make the best use of what you have and try to guess what your opponent is planning. A good idea at the start of a game can change everything at the end. Thinking several moves ahead, reasoning logically and changing plans when the situation shifts: that's what these games train. They're aimed more at kids aged 7 or 8, although some very simple ones can be played earlier. Chess and checkers rely on the same skills: a child who enjoys these games may want to try them too, on a real board.

genre.defense.titre_seo: Free tower defense games for kids: plan and protect
genre.defense.description_seo: Place your towers at the right bend and stop the waves of intruders: free tower defense games for kids on a phone, tablet or computer, then offline.
genre.defense.intro: Here's how it works: a line of little invaders moves along a path, and you have to stop them before they reach your castle, your garden or your base. To do that, you set up towers, traps or guards in the right places, then upgrade them from wave to wave. No realistic violence: the intruders are pushed back, slowed down or put to sleep. Planning, managing resources, studying the terrain: spotting the bend where your best defense should go changes everything. These games suit kids from about 6 or 7. Lost a wave? By looking back at where your defenses were placed, you quickly see what was missing.

genre.gestion.h1: Management and tycoon games for kids
genre.gestion.titre_seo: Free tycoon games for kids: run a shop, a farm or a zoo
genre.gestion.description_seo: Serve customers, harvest, sell and save up: free management games where the money is only pretend, on a phone, tablet or computer, and offline next time.
genre.gestion.intro: Spend right away or save for later? In a management game, you're in charge of a little world: a shop, a farm, a restaurant, a zoo or a town. You serve customers, harvest, buy, sell and decide how to use the game's money, which is always pretend, to grow your business. They're also called tycoon games, after a word for a powerful business owner. Math, organization, time management and the idea of a budget are learned hands-on. A little shop can be run from 5 or 6; businesses where you need to count and plan ahead suit kids from 7 or 8 better. For parents, it's a ready-made way into a chat about pocket money and saving.

genre.simulation.titre_seo: Free care and simulation games for kids: animals and jobs
genre.simulation.description_seo: Care for an animal, bandage a scrape, cook a meal: free simulation games on a phone, tablet or PC, and playable offline after your first game.
genre.simulation.intro: Taking the place of someone who looks after others or does a real job: that's the heart of simulation games. You can feed, brush and care for an animal, bandage a small scrape, cook a meal or drive a vehicle, following the steps in the right order. Real life is simplified and told with tenderness: you understand what a living creature needs and why each step matters. Empathy, a sense of responsibility, patience and attention to detail develop naturally. From 4 or 5, you mostly move forward by tapping and dragging. Before a visit to the vet or the doctor, these games make the gestures familiar and can reassure a worried child.

genre.creation.titre_seo: Free dress-up and design games for kids: create your style
genre.creation.description_seo: Choose the outfit, the hairstyle and the accessories: free dress-up and design games on a phone, tablet or computer, even offline afterwards.
genre.creation.intro: You decide everything. Clothes, hairstyles and accessories for a character or an animal, decorating a bedroom, a cake or a card, building a hero from head to toe: these games give your ideas free rein. Very often there's no right or wrong answer; the fun is in trying combinations, comparing and creating something that feels like you. Your eye for colors, shapes and matching grows without you even thinking about it. You mostly play by tapping and moving items around, so kids aged 4 or 5 pick them up easily. Telling the story of your character afterwards, their outfit and their personality, extends the game with a lovely moment of storytelling.

genre.construction.titre_seo: Free building and sandbox games for kids to play online
genre.construction.description_seo: Stack, assemble, build a bridge that stays up: free building and sandbox games for kids on a phone, tablet or computer, then offline once opened.
genre.construction.intro: A sandbox game doesn't always set a goal: blocks, pieces or tools are at your disposal, and you build whatever you want. A house, a bridge, a tower that has to stay standing, a whole village or a wacky machine. Others offer challenges, like building a structure that's strong enough or reaching an exact height: then you have to test, fail and fix. Imagination, a sense of balance and a first intuition of how things hold together develop with each attempt. Free building appeals from 4 or 5, architecture challenges a little later. Giving a grown-up a tour of your creation makes you proud and means explaining your ideas.

genre.musique.titre_seo: Free music and rhythm games for kids: tap to the beat
genre.musique.description_seo: Tap to the beat, replay a melody, recognize the instruments: free music and rhythm games for kids on a phone, tablet or PC, then playable offline.
genre.musique.intro: These games are played with your ears as much as your fingers. You tap at the exact moment a note arrives, repeat a short melody in order, recognize an instrument or compose your own tune by choosing sounds. The tempo guides everything: stay in rhythm and the successes keep coming. Listening, memory for sounds and coordination improve together. Simple listening games suit kids around 4 or 5, while fast challenges appeal to older ones. It's best to play with the sound on, with headphones if needed. And when the screen goes off, the music goes on: singing or clapping together keeps the fun going.

genre.societe.titre_seo: Free online board games and card games for kids to play
genre.societe.description_seo: Boards, pieces, dice and cards: all the fun of tabletop games, free for kids on a phone, tablet or PC, and playable offline once you've opened them.
genre.societe.intro: Pieces moving across a board, dice to roll, cards to draw, flip or play at the right moment: board and card games bring back the fun of playing around a table. Classic rules or brand-new inventions, they almost always mix luck and thinking. You learn to follow a rule, wait your turn, count and guess what the other player will do. The simplest ones can be played from 5 or 6. No game is played against strangers on the internet: you play against the computer, or with several players on the same screen when the game allows it. Side by side, you also learn to lose with a smile.

genre.coloriage.titre_seo: Free online coloring pages and drawing games for kids
genre.coloriage.description_seo: From age 3, color with your fingertip and draw without going over the lines: free coloring games on a phone, tablet or computer, then offline.
genre.coloriage.intro: Pick a color, tap an area, and the drawing comes to life. Pictures to color, shapes to trace, patterns to complete or a blank page to fill with your own ideas: anything goes. No pencil going over the lines, no marker drying out, and you can change your mind as often as you like. Creativity, precise movements, color recognition and calm concentration are all there. You don't need to read, which opens these games to kids from age 3; older ones often prefer detailed pictures or free drawing. They offer a real moment of calm, and nothing stops you from copying your favorite drawing onto a sheet of paper afterwards.

genre.role.titre_seo: Free role-playing games for kids: quests and level-ups
genre.role.description_seo: Play a hero who gains experience and new skills quest after quest: free role-playing games for kids on a phone, tablet or PC, then offline too.
genre.role.intro: Your character grows along with you. Through quests and challenges, they gain experience, become stronger or more skillful, discover new talents and equip useful items. The game builds up over time: choices made at the start, like which qualities to develop first, shape everything that follows. Reading, decision-making, planning and perseverance all work together. These games often require reading fairly rich texts and menus, which makes them more comfortable around 8 or 9, even if some can be played earlier. The urge to play “just one more level” is strong: it's best to agree on how long to play before starting.

genre.autre.titre_seo: Original, one-of-a-kind games for kids, free to play
genre.autre.description_seo: Games with invented rules that don't fit into any category: free surprises to play on a phone, tablet or PC, then offline once you've opened them.
genre.autre.intro: Some games refuse to fit into a single category. They mix several ways of playing, invent a rule never seen before or rest on an idea too unusual to be filed with puzzles, races or quizzes. This is where they end up. Expect surprises: each game has its own rules, explained in a few words on screen at the start. It's hard to say in advance what they train, since they're all different; what they have in common is that they call for curiosity and a desire to try something new. The recommended age, shown for each game, remains the best guide. If a rule seems strange at first, give it two or three rounds: that's often when the game reveals its trick.

univers.ferme.titre_seo: Free farm games for kids: farm animals and harvests
univers.ferme.description_seo: Cows, hens, tractors and vegetable patches: country life in free farm games for kids on a phone, tablet or computer, then playable offline later.
univers.ferme.intro: Where do milk, eggs and market vegetables come from? On the farm, every animal and every field has its role. These games take place in the farmyard, the barn, the vegetable garden or the fields, and come in all sorts of forms: memory, racing, management or puzzles. You feed the animals, collect the eggs, count the chicks or drive a tractor. Kids learn to recognize familiar animals, their sounds and their young (calf, lamb, foal), and to follow the rhythm of sowing and harvesting. Younger players love finding animals they already know; older ones especially enjoy organizing challenges, when everything has to run at once.

univers.chevaux.titre_seo: Free horse and pony games for kids: riding and grooming
univers.chevaux.description_seo: Brush, care for and dress up your pony, then gallop away: free horse riding games on a phone, tablet or computer that you can replay offline.
univers.chevaux.intro: The world of horses holds a special place for many kids, and it has its own page. The games take place at the stable, in the paddock or at the riding school: depending on the game, you get a pony ready and brush it, choose its outfit, feed it, gallop, clear jumps or answer riding quiz questions. Riding vocabulary slips in naturally (coat, mane, halter, trot, gallop), along with grooming routines and respect for the animal. Young riders and dreamers who have never been near a pony each have something to enjoy: the former will be proud to explain the words they recognize, the latter may discover a wish to try a first pony ride.

univers.compagnie.h1: Pet games: dogs, cats and more
univers.compagnie.titre_seo: Free pet games for kids: dogs, cats, bunnies and more
univers.compagnie.description_seo: Dreaming of a puppy or a kitten? Free games to feed, walk and look after your pet, on a phone, tablet or PC, and playable offline afterwards.
univers.compagnie.intro: Dogs, cats, rabbits, hamsters, budgies or goldfish: these animals share our homes, and they're the heroes of these games. Depending on the game, you feed a kitten, walk a dog, find a hidden hamster or care for an injured paw. Behind the fun lies a simple idea: an animal has needs (eating, drinking, sleeping, playing, being cared for), and you have to think about them every day, even when you have other things to do. Kids who dream of a pet get some practice, and those who already have one recognize familiar routines. Before adopting, these games open a conversation about the responsibilities that come with a real animal.

univers.sauvages.h1: Wild animal games: savanna, jungle and forest
univers.sauvages.titre_seo: Free wild animal games: savanna, jungle and polar ice
univers.sauvages.description_seo: Lions, elephants, monkeys, polar bears: go and meet wild animals in free games for kids on a phone, tablet or PC, and find them again offline.
univers.sauvages.intro: Every habitat has its residents. Lions and giraffes on the savanna; monkeys and parrots in the jungle; squirrels and foxes in the forest; polar bears on the sea ice. These games take you to watch animals in their homes, through observation, memory, racing or thinking games. You learn to recognize species, match them with their habitat and notice how they move or feed. The animals are shown gently, with no frightening hunting scenes. What about you: which animal would you love to see with your own eyes, and how far would you have to travel to meet it?

univers.dinosaures.titre_seo: Free dinosaur and prehistoric games for kids to play
univers.dinosaures.description_seo: Meet tyrannosaurs, triceratops and mammoths in free dinosaur games for kids on a phone, tablet or computer, then play them offline once opened.
univers.dinosaures.intro: Their size, their impressive names and the mystery of their disappearance: dinosaurs are fascinating. Everything here happens in their time, and more broadly in prehistory: volcanoes, giant ferns, eggs about to hatch, fossil digs, mammoths and early humans around the fire. Observation, memory or reflexes come into play, and a few species names end up sticking, as does the difference between herbivores and carnivores. The dinosaurs stay friendly: no menacing jaws or scary chases. A fact to impress everyone with: the great dinosaurs and the first humans never lived at the same time. More than sixty million years separate them.

univers.ocean.titre_seo: Free ocean games for kids: fish, diving and coral reefs
univers.ocean.description_seo: Put on your mask: fish, dolphins, turtles and coral are waiting for you in free sea games on a phone, tablet or computer, then offline as well.
univers.ocean.intro: Beneath the surface, the ocean hides a world of colors: coral reefs, schools of fish, jellyfish, octopuses, turtles and whales. Swim between obstacles, feed the fish, explore a shipwreck, build a sandcastle or collect seashells: depending on the game, the adventure happens underwater or on the beach. You discover the diversity of sea life, from tiny plankton to great whales, and you realize along the way that a clean sea is a healthy sea. Kids who spend their vacations by the water and those who have never seen the sea both feel at home here. Naming the creatures you meet, in English or in another language, adds a game within the game.

univers.espace.h1: Space games: rockets, planets and stars
univers.espace.titre_seo: Free space games for kids: rockets, planets, astronauts
univers.espace.description_seo: Fly a rocket, visit the planets, dodge the comets: free space games for kids on a phone, tablet or computer, even offline after your first game.
univers.espace.intro: Rockets, astronauts, planets, asteroids and space stations: off to the stars. From one game to the next, you pilot a spaceship, dodge meteorites, land a module on the Moon or connect the stars of a constellation. Space suits fast reflex and aiming games just as well as calm puzzles where you take time to think. Game after game, the order of the planets around the Sun, the difference between a star and a planet, or the idea that an astronaut floats inside the station become familiar. An evening spent looking at the sky, far from city lights, is a chance to find the Moon and a few bright stars, and to talk about them together.

univers.fantasy.h1: Magic and fantasy games: fairies, wizards and dragons
univers.fantasy.titre_seo: Free magic games: fairies, wizards, dragons and unicorns
univers.fantasy.description_seo: Wands, potions, unicorns and enchanted castles: free magic games for kids on a phone, tablet or computer that you can keep playing offline later.
univers.fantasy.intro: Fairies, wizards, unicorns, dragons, fizzing potions and enchanted forests: here, magic is part of everyday life. You cast spells, mix strange ingredients, help a fairy creature or travel through an imaginary kingdom. Behind this setting are games that are very different from one another: strategy, puzzles, defense, adventure or creation. The magic stays bright and cheerful, with no unsettling witchcraft. These worlds spark the imagination and make you want to invent your own stories. A magic spell you made up, a creature drawn on a sheet of paper with its secret powers: the best follow-up to a game is often the one you imagine yourself.

univers.chevaliers.h1: Knight games: castles and the Middle Ages
univers.chevaliers.titre_seo: Free knight games for kids: castles and the Middle Ages
univers.chevaliers.description_seo: Castles, tournaments, coats of arms and blacksmiths: live the Middle Ages in free knight games on a phone, tablet or computer, then replay them offline.
univers.chevaliers.intro: Ramparts, drawbridges, coats of arms, tournaments and village markets: welcome to the age of knights. Defend a castle, build a tower, recognize coats of arms or take on the challenges of a young squire: the Middle Ages are told at a child's level, with their trades (blacksmith, miller, builder), castle life and festivals, without bloody battles. Strategy, organization and patience are often in the spotlight, because you build and protect more than you fight. The most curious pick up words along the way that they'll meet again in class, the day the Middle Ages are on the curriculum: keep, moat, lord, armor, minstrel.

univers.pirates.h1: Pirate games: treasure, ships and islands
univers.pirates.titre_seo: Free pirate games for kids: treasure hunts and ships
univers.pirates.description_seo: Hoist the sails, read the map and find the treasure chest: free pirate games for kids on a phone, tablet or computer, to play again offline later.
univers.pirates.intro: Black flag, parrot on the shoulder, treasure map and mysterious island: all aboard! Sail between reefs, decipher a map, search for a buried chest or protect your ship from storms: that's the plan. These pirates are fictional characters, more pranksters than villains. While playing, you find your way, follow directions (north, south, left, right), count gold coins and keep your eyes open. It's the perfect setting for fans of riddles and treasure hunts. A little idea for home: hide an object, draw the map that leads to it and let the child follow it, like a real captain.

univers.monstres.titre_seo: Free monster games for kids: funny, friendly creatures
univers.monstres.description_seo: Friendly monsters and wacky creatures: free games that make you smile rather than feel scared, on a phone, tablet or computer, then offline.
univers.monstres.intro: Floppy horns, three eyes, spots of every color and lots of humor: that's the portrait of the monsters on this page. These imaginary creatures are heroes, companions or clumsy opponents in arcade, adventure, strategy or building games. The goal isn't to scare: you discover them as funny, always hungry, shy or lovable. Playing with them can even help some kids tame their bedtime fears, by showing that a strange creature can be kind. Inventing, feeding or putting together a monster also works the imagination and sense of humor. For a sensitive child, it's a good starting point: here, you laugh at things that might feel worrying elsewhere.

univers.robots.titre_seo: Free robot games for kids: machines and the future
univers.robots.description_seo: A robot to guide step by step, machines to fix, the city of tomorrow to imagine: free games on a phone, tablet or PC, to launch again offline.
univers.robots.intro: Gears, circuits, blinking lights and cities of tomorrow: make way for robots and technology. Guide a robot step by step, repair a machine, assemble parts or imagine life in the future: this theme calls for games where you think in order, plan a sequence of actions, spot a mistake and try again differently. It's a first introduction, without a single line of code, to the logic behind programming. The robots are helpful companions. To carry on without a screen, a grown-up can turn into a robot: the child “programs” them out loud (two steps forward, turn right) and checks whether they end up in the right place.

univers.nature.titre_seo: Free nature and garden games for kids: plants and bugs
univers.nature.description_seo: Sow, water, watch the insects and follow the seasons: free nature and gardening games for kids on a phone, tablet or computer, then offline as well.
univers.nature.intro: A seed sprouting, a bee gathering nectar, a forest changing color in the fall: nature close to home is the subject of these games. Depending on the game, you garden, water, watch insects, listen to frogs or follow a plant as it grows. This theme welcomes calm games where you take your time as well as faster challenges. It helps you understand nature's cycles: what a plant needs to grow, the role of pollinators, the rhythm of the seasons. Kids who like to observe and take care of things feel at home here. A pot of soil and a few radish seeds on the windowsill are then enough to see it all for real: the harvest arrives in a few weeks.

univers.cuisine.h1: Cooking games: cakes, recipes and baking
univers.cuisine.titre_seo: Free cooking games for kids: bake cakes, follow recipes
univers.cuisine.description_seo: Make cakes, pizzas or smoothies step by step: free cooking games for kids on a phone, tablet or computer, and playable offline afterwards as well.
univers.cuisine.intro: Flour, eggs, fruit, frosting and chocolate chips: the screen becomes a kitchen counter. Follow a recipe, decorate a cake, serve hurried customers or sort foods into groups: each game has its own way of getting into the kitchen. The order of the steps, remembering ingredients, measuring quantities and, when orders pile up, organization all come into play. You can also talk about balanced eating, fruits and vegetables in season or dishes from other countries. A simple recipe made together after the game, like a fruit salad or pancakes, takes you from the screen to the real kitchen, tasting included.

univers.vehicules.h1: Car, truck, train and plane games
univers.vehicules.titre_seo: Free vehicle games for kids: cars, trucks and planes
univers.vehicules.description_seo: Cars, tractors, trains, boats, planes and diggers: take the controls in free vehicle games for kids on a phone, tablet or computer, then offline too.
univers.vehicules.intro: Everything that rolls, flies or sails has its place here: race cars, fire trucks, buses, trains, boats, planes, helicopters and construction vehicles. Races, skill courses, traffic puzzles or building games: the ways to play vary. Driving around obstacles sharpens reflexes; parking a truck or organizing a crossroads gets you thinking about space and trajectories. Recognizing each vehicle and imitating its sound delights the youngest, while older kids go for the toughest courses. Traffic lights, crosswalks, seat belts fastened: these games also open the door to a first conversation about road safety.

univers.sport.h1: Games to discover sports and their rules
univers.sport.titre_seo: Free sports-themed games: rules, disciplines and records
univers.sport.description_seo: Referees, belts, relays and records: free games for kids to discover sports and their rules, on a phone, tablet or computer, then playable offline.
univers.sport.intro: On this page, sports are the subject of the game, whatever the way of playing: you can compete in an event, but also answer questions about a discipline, find the equipment for each sport or learn the rules of a match. Soccer, swimming, skiing, gymnastics, track and field or martial arts: each sport has its vocabulary, its moves and its values. You learn what a referee, a belt, a relay or a record is, and you discover team spirit and respect for your opponent. A game about the sport a child plays often makes the next practice more concrete; another may spark the wish to try a new activity.

univers.monde.h1: World geography games: countries and flags
univers.monde.titre_seo: Free geography games for kids: countries, flags and maps
univers.monde.description_seo: Flags, capitals, continents and traditions: travel around the world with free games for kids on a phone, tablet or computer, and even offline later.
univers.monde.intro: Where is Japan? Which flag has a maple leaf on it? In which country do people eat tacos? These games invite you to travel from one continent to another. Place countries on a map, match flags, discover monuments, typical animals, dishes or festivals from elsewhere: geography becomes a game. Curiosity, spatial awareness and memory get a workout, and future geography lessons will feel more familiar. The trickiest questions, about capitals or rare flags, suit good readers, around age 8. At the end of the journey, one idea remains: the world is vast and varied, and every culture has its own customs.

univers.histoire.h1: History games: eras, inventions and great voyages
univers.histoire.titre_seo: Free history games for kids: past eras and inventions
univers.histoire.description_seo: Travel back in time, from the pyramids to the great explorers, with free history games for kids on a phone, tablet or computer, then offline.
univers.histoire.intro: Going back in time is possible, for the length of a game. From the Egypt of the pharaohs to the great explorations, by way of ancient Rome, these games take place in a past era or tell the story of how an invention came about. They help place events in relation to one another, imagine how people lived long ago and see that today's world was built little by little. Wars and dark times aren't shown: the focus is on daily life, discoveries and monuments. These games speak mostly to kids who are starting to study history at school, and to anyone who wonders how people lived before electricity or cars.

univers.corps.titre_seo: Free human body games for kids: health, hygiene, senses
univers.corps.description_seo: How does your body work? Skeleton, five senses, teeth to brush: free games to find out, on a phone, tablet or computer, then playable offline.
univers.corps.intro: How does the heart beat? What are bones for? Why brush your teeth morning and night? These games help you discover the human body and how to take care of it. Rebuild a skeleton, name the parts of the body, test your five senses or learn good hygiene habits, like handwashing: the explanations stay simple, with no upsetting images. Putting words to what you feel and adopting good habits (eating well, moving, getting enough sleep) comes more naturally. These games don't replace a doctor's advice. An experiment to try afterwards: put your hand on your heart at rest, then after a minute of jumping in place, and feel the difference.

univers.ville.titre_seo: Free job games for kids: firefighter, doctor, vet and more
univers.ville.description_seo: Firefighter, baker, vet or mail carrier: discover the jobs that keep a city running in free games on a phone, tablet or computer, offline after a first visit.
univers.ville.intro: Who puts out fires, who treats dogs, who delivers the mail, who bakes bread before dawn? The city and the people who keep it running are at the heart of these games. You take on a job, run a shop, direct traffic or help the residents of a neighborhood. Everyone's role, the vocabulary of jobs and the rules of living together (waiting your turn, crossing at the right place, helping out) start to make sense. The eternal question “what do you want to be when you grow up?” finds plenty of food for thought. A parent can also take the chance to describe their own work in simple words.

univers.fetes.h1: Holiday and seasonal games: Christmas, Easter, Halloween
univers.fetes.titre_seo: Free Christmas, Easter and Halloween games for kids
univers.fetes.description_seo: Decorated trees, chocolate eggs, pumpkins and snowmen: free seasonal games for kids on a phone, tablet or computer, and playable offline afterwards.
univers.fetes.intro: Snowmen in winter, egg hunts in spring, sandcastles in summer, fallen leaves and pumpkins in the fall: these games follow the calendar. Decorate a tree, prepare a birthday party, fill a sack with presents or dress up for carnival: each season has its game. Younger kids learn to find their way through the year, name the seasons and months, and understand that holidays come back year after year. They also discover that traditions change from one country to another. Halloween pumpkins stay smiling. Bringing out a seasonal game at the right time, when the view out the window matches it, makes it even more meaningful.

univers.contes.titre_seo: Free fairy tale and legend games for kids to play online
univers.contes.description_seo: Once upon a time there were wolves, giants and mermaids: free games inspired by fairy tales, on a phone, tablet or computer, offline once opened.
univers.contes.intro: Once upon a time, there was a wolf knocking at the door, a pumpkin that turned into a carriage, a giant at the top of a beanstalk. These games draw on traditional fairy tales and legends from all over the world, or invent new ones with the same ingredients: a deep forest, a castle, trials and a happy ending. You meet characters you know from books, and others you'll discover later. A love of stories grows, along with vocabulary and an understanding of how stories are built (a beginning, obstacles, a solution). These games go well with bedtime reading: reread the original tale after playing, then compare the two versions.

univers.abstrait.h1: Abstract games: shapes, colors and patterns
univers.abstrait.titre_seo: Free abstract games: shapes, colors and geometry puzzles
univers.abstrait.description_seo: Shapes, colors, patterns and lines, with no story or characters: free abstract games on a phone, tablet or PC, and offline after your first game.
univers.abstrait.intro: No heroes, no scenery, just shapes, colors, lines and patterns: these games get straight to the point. You line up colored pieces, rotate geometric shapes, fill a grid, guide a ball or repeat a sequence. With no story to distract you, all your attention goes to the rule and the solution. Logic, perception of shapes and colors, anticipation and concentration are constantly in use. Young children learn to sort and recognize a square or a triangle; older ones look for challenging brain teasers. Good to know: a short game can serve as a warm-up for the mind before homework.

univers.autre.h1: Games with unexpected settings and themes
univers.autre.titre_seo: Free games with original worlds and one-of-a-kind settings
univers.autre.description_seo: Settings that don't fit any usual theme: free games with original, unexpected worlds, on a phone, tablet or PC, then playable offline as well.
univers.autre.intro: Not animals, not space, not cooking, nor any of the site's other themes: the setting of these games is too original, too mixed or simply too unexpected to fit into a box. Everyday objects coming to life, a miniature world, a strange dream or an idea never seen before: anything can happen. This page works a bit like a drawer full of surprises. Its content therefore varies a lot, in style as much as in difficulty; each game's recommended age and description remain the best guides for choosing. If you like being surprised and trying new things, this is the place to dig around.

age.3-4.titre_seo: Easy free games for 3 and 4 year olds: tap and play
age.3-4.description_seo: At 3 and 4, kids play with a fingertip: colors, shapes, animals and sounds in easy free games on a phone, tablet or computer, then offline too.
age.3-4.intro: At 3 or 4, a child discovers the screen with their fingers: they tap, swipe and watch what happens. The games gathered here are recommended from this age. They rely on simple gestures, clearly visible pictures and short instructions, to recognize colors, shapes, animals or sounds, match pairs or count a few objects. Having a grown-up nearby is still valuable: reading the instruction out loud, encouraging, naming what appears on screen. At this age, a few minutes of play is plenty. And since a game opened once with the internet can then be replayed offline, it can also fill a car trip or a moment in a waiting room.

age.5-6.titre_seo: Games for kids aged 5 and 6: free learning games to play
age.5-6.description_seo: Letters, numbers, memory, logic and first challenges: games recommended from age 5 or 6, on a phone, tablet or PC, then offline once opened.
age.5-6.intro: Between 5 and 6, children are starting school in earnest: they recognize letters, begin to read, count higher and higher and love taking on challenges. All the games on this page are recommended from age 5 or 6. Many combine several small rules, level-by-level progress and stars to earn, which makes you want to try again to do better. Memory, attention, logic, precise movements and the first things learned at school all get a chance to practice. Some instructions still need a little help with reading: a grown-up or an older sibling can read them the first time, then let the child spread their wings.

age.7-8.titre_seo: Free online games for kids aged 7 and 8: a step up
age.7-8.description_seo: Riddles, strategy, reflexes and general knowledge: more demanding games, recommended from age 7 or 8, on a phone, tablet or PC, then offline.
age.7-8.intro: Reading a short instruction alone, counting with ease, following a rule with several steps: around 7 or 8, most children can do this, and the games for this age group make the most of it. Longer levels, puzzles that take several moves, time management, little strategies or general knowledge questions: the difficulty goes up a notch. Reasoning, concentration, speed and perseverance improve, because beating a tough level sometimes takes several tries. These games are happily played independently, with a grown-up nearby, ready to admire the level finally beaten.

age.9+.h1: Games for kids aged 9 and up
age.9+.titre_seo: Free games for kids aged 9 and up: real challenges to beat
age.9+.description_seo: For ages 9 and up, free games that put up a fight: brain teasers, strategy, speed and trivia on a phone, tablet or PC, even offline later on.
age.9+.intro: From age 9, players like a game that pushes back. The games recommended from this age offer brain teasers that require thinking several moves ahead, strategy and management, courses that demand precise reflexes, or tougher quizzes. The difficulty rises from level to level, and beating your own record becomes a goal in itself. Planning, logical thinking, handling mistakes and patience come out stronger. These games are still designed for kids: no realistic violence or frightening scenes, no contact with strangers. Teens and adults can test themselves too, and a player this age is perfectly entitled to go back to games for younger kids to relax.
